Subject: Order form redlines — output/training exclusions and productization gate

Markus / Laura / Connor,

Thanks again for the demo this week. We're excited to move forward with the PoC. Before procurement can sign the order form we need to clear a few legal concerns raised by our internal counsel (cc'd). High level: Novalink needs explicit guarantees that our Customer Outputs will not be used to train models, and we want an explicit productization gate so Redwood cannot commercially productize or redistribute outputs derived from our customer data.

Attached: Novalink_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf with the clauses we redlined. Key asks: 
- No training: Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or any identifiable Customer Data to train base or fine-tuned models without explicit written opt-in per account.
- Output ownership: Novalink retains exclusive ownership of Customer Outputs; Redwood gets no rights to re-use or sell those outputs.
- Feedback license: If Redwood wants any limited feedback license it must be narrowly scoped (bug fixes, service reliability) and revocable.
- Auditability: we need telemetry/audit evidence of how data was used and retained.

We aim to finalize commercial terms by end of next week; procurement needs clear wording to present to finance. Can you have your legal and product teams review and propose alternative language that preserves our rights while allowing Redwood to operate?

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — really appreciate the clear redlines. Good summary. Labelling internal owners: Laura (account lead) and Connor (ops & deployment) are on the thread; I'll loop legal (Ben) next.

High-level reply from product/sales perspective: Redwood's core position is that we do not use identifiable Customer Outputs as training data for public base models. Where we've historically seen friction is around telemetry and aggregated signal used to improve serving quality and security (e.g., prompt safety, latency optimizations). We think there are three workable levers: 

1) Customer Outputs ownership: we can agree to explicit language that Customer Outputs remain customer property and Redwood will not assert ownership.
2) Training carveout: Redwood proposes a narrow carveout that allows use of de-identified, aggregated telemetry strictly for service improvement, with an explicit prohibition on feeding Customer Outputs into model training pipelines used for commercial models.
3) Feedback license: a time-limited, revocable license for operational feedback (debugging, quality improvement) — not for productization.

I'll ask Ben to propose crisp legal language for these points and attach a counter-redline. Proposed next steps: Ben to send counter redline today; schedule a 30-min legal sync with Novalink counsel (cc Miriam) on Monday 29 May to close language. Also Connor can provide a short doc on telemetry/audit proof points.

—Markus

Alex / Miriam,

Thanks for the redlines and for flagging Novalink's priorities. Attached is Redwood_Counter_Redlines_v3.pdf and a short "Proposed_Legal_Text_Productization.docx" with suggested clause text. Below is the operative summary and proposed legal wording (high level) so your team can triage before the call.

Summary of Redwood's proposal (short):
- Customer Outputs: Customer retains exclusive ownership of Customer Outputs. Redwood expressly disclaims ownership and will not sell or redistribute Customer Outputs.
- Training & Model Use: Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve base models or any models used for commercial offering unless Customer provides a separate, explicit opt-in agreement.
- Aggregate Telemetry: Redwood may collect de-identified aggregate telemetry derived from service usage (latency metrics, anonymized prompt length distributions, error rates) for the purpose of monitoring and improving the service. Such telemetry will be aggregated across customers where feasible and will not include Customer Outputs or any data that could be re-associated with a specific customer.
- Feedback License: If Customer elects to provide explicit feedback (bug reports, labelled examples), Redwood may use such feedback only to fix or improve the specific contracted service instance for Customer and will not use it to train models for general commercial release absent an opt-in. The license is revocable by Customer upon 30 days' notice.
- Audit & Retention: Redwood will provide telemetry and audit logs relevant to the engagement (token volumes, request ids, timestamps, region) for a mutually agreed retention period and will support reasonable audit requests tied to the engagement.

Proposed sample clause (for legal review):
"Customer Outputs" means text, images or other content generated by the Service in response to Customer inputs. Except as otherwise set forth in a written Order Form, Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Outputs. Redwood will not, without Customer's prior written consent, (i) use Customer Outputs to train or improve any model that is part of Redwood's public or commercial model offerings, or (ii) sell, sublicense, or otherwise commercialize Customer Outputs. Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for monitoring and service improvement, provided that such telemetry does not contain Customer Outputs or any information reasonably capable of being re-associated with Customer.

Please review the attached counter-redlines; key open questions we expect on the call: specific retention period for audit logs, what counts as "de-identified" for Novalink, and narrowness of the feedback license scope.

If Monday doesn't work, propose two time slots and we'll accommodate.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
